channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: A local world model you can steer with WASD just landed on Hugging Face — and it runs on an RTX 3060
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: LucidML turns a single image into a playable video you steer in real time — a 630M-parameter world model trained from scratch, with open weights and a live demo that runs on consumer GPUs.

item.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking its flights — the first US carrier to draw the line
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: United rewrote its Contract of Carriage on November 11 to bar AI agents from buying tickets, seats or upgrades — and says it can cancel any reservation an agent touches. Searching is still allowed; checkout is not.

item.title: British AI chip startup Fractile raises $720M at a $7B valuation, with UK state backing
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Fractile, a London- and Bristol-based startup designing chips for AI inference, has raised $720 million at a $7 billion valuation — with the UK government’s Sovereign AI fund and the British Business Bank in the round. The catch: the company has never shipped a chip, and the state won’t say how much of its own money is in the deal.

item.title: Palantir's Alex Karp says he's a lifelong Democrat and the company is 'essentially progressive'
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Days after the Democrats' midterm wins, Palantir CEO Alex Karp told Politico he has 'been a Democrat my whole life,' called the company's products 'essentially progressive,' and opened the door to backing a Democrat in 2028 — a sharp turn for the chief of the Trump administration's closest AI contractor.

item.title: DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2: DNA variant predictions, cell by cell
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how a DNA variant changes gene activity in one specific cell type at a time, recovering nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor. Non-commercial access is open now through the AlphaGenome API.

item.title: Your AI coding agent may have leaked your API keys to GitHub — how to find and purge them
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apiiro found 2,539 real secrets in public repos after Claude Code's "don't ask again" button saved them verbatim. Audit your own repos with Gitleaks and TruffleHog, purge leaked secrets from git history, and stop it happening again.

item.title: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' Is Quietly Leaking Secrets Into Public Repos
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Approving a command with 'don't ask again' saves it — tokens and all — into a file Claude Code doesn't protect with your project's .gitignore. Apiiro found over 100,000 copies of that file on public GitHub, more than 1,100 of them holding real secrets.

item.title: Runway open-sources Praxis-1: the robot model that learned to act by watching video
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Runway has released Praxis-1, its 27-billion-parameter world action model, with open weights under Apache 2.0. Trained first on internet video and then on robot data, it predicts the next video frames and the actions to match — and tops NVIDIA’s RoboLab-120 leaderboard at 46.2%.

item.title: Amazon’s Ring launches a flying home camera and a $1,000 patrol robot
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Amazon’s Ring unveiled Ring Robotics on November 10: the Ring Drone Cam, a $249.99 indoor flying camera, and the Ring Rover Cam, a $999.99 wheeled patrol robot for businesses. Both are navigated by a new AI Pilot system — but the drone can’t ship until the FCC authorizes it.

item.title: WSJ: Nvidia board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang as a second affair surfaces
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reports, three days after it opened an investigation into an alleged Chinese spy operation targeting him. A second reported relationship — with a direct report — has turned a national-security inquiry into a workplace one, and shares fell about 8% after hours.

item.title: OpenAI board member Paul Christiano: 'high risk of an AI takeover within the next 3 years'
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At Toronto’s Hinton Lectures, OpenAI foundation board member Paul Christiano warned of a high risk of AI takeover within three years — a coin flip, he said, if AI is developed as fast as possible. A 68-second clip hit Reddit on Wednesday, and the top replies were skeptical, not scared.

item.title: Hands-on with shadcn's improve: audit your codebase with your best model, execute with your cheapest
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: improve (shadcn/improve, 10,755 stars, MIT) turns your best model into a senior advisor: it audits any codebase across nine categories and writes self-contained implementation plans for cheaper models to execute — without touching a line of source. Install it, run /improve quick, and close the loop.

item.title: Nominal raises $240M at a $3B valuation to bring AI to hardware engineering
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Nominal, the AI platform for testing aircraft, reactors, and robots, raised a $240 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation — tripling its value in eight months as defense contractors and industrial giants buy into its hardware-intelligence pitch.

item.title: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a model that answers in probabilities instead of prose
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google's new Decisions API runs Gemini Decision 1, a model that scores up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric questions in a single pass — no text generated, no output tokens billed. Reddit's first reaction: useful, but the benchmarks are Google's own.

item.title: Design with an elephant, review with a goldfish: hands-on with Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model makes your coding agent design before it builds: an elephant drafts the spec, fresh zero-context goldfish reviewers attack it, and you approve it. Install takes two commands; the review runs in five phases. Every install command verified.

item.title: A Claude-built archive of 300,000 military board decisions is now evidence in a federal lawsuit against Trump and the Pentagon
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A veterans’ legal nonprofit sued the President and the Pentagon on November 10 after building a searchable archive of 300,000 military board decisions with Claude. The complaint uses the archive to show the Defense Department’s own records site can’t find its own cases.

item.title: Stop shipping generic AI websites: hands-on with taste-skill, the design-taste skill for coding agents
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: taste-skill (Leonxlnx/taste-skill, 113,400 stars, MIT) gives coding agents art direction: dealt palettes, one design system, real product UI, and a browser checker that refuses to ship a page with open failures. Install it, deal a design, build a page, and run the gate — every command verified.

item.title: Helsing unveils Clarity: AI that recommends military targets, with a human's name on every decision
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Helsing unveiled Clarity in Berlin: hundreds of AI agents fuse sensor feeds and intelligence into target recommendations — but nothing reaches a weapon system until a named human officer authorises it. Europe's answer to Palantir's Maven, and the sovereignty pitch is the point.

item.title: Give your coding agent the whole repo: pack any codebase for an LLM with Repomix
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pasting files into a chat window one at a time is how context goes to die. Repomix packs a whole repo into one LLM-ready file — with token counts, a secret scan, and a compression mode. Every number in this guide was measured, not quoted.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 maxed its usage to make a 55-second motion-graphics film — and Reddit calls it scary decent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Reddit creator gave Claude Fable 5.2 a premise and a day. Four concepts and 13 review rounds later, a 55-second motion-graphics film came back — written entirely as code. The thread’s verdict: “scary decent.”

item.title: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2: DNA predictions tuned to individual cell types
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA variants act in specific cell types, not tissue averages — trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it finds nearly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor.

item.title: TSMC approves up to $1 billion in stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: TSMC's board approved up to $500 million in Anthropic shares and up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock — the world's biggest chipmaker is buying into the two labs that drive demand for its most advanced chips, and the line between supplier and shareholder just got thinner.

item.title: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' backdoor hides in fewer than 10 dormant neurons — and needs no retraining
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft researchers have shown that reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in a language model can turn an AI agent built on it into a sleeper backdoor — no retraining required, and the model still passes its safety evals. The trigger can be as ordinary as a date.

item.title: Rumor: NVIDIA reportedly cancels the 24GB RTX 5080 launch as GDDR7 memory costs soar
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: NVIDIA has reportedly told its board partners the 24GB RTX 5080 won't launch in January, killed by the price of 3GB GDDR7 chips — and the 16GB card it was supposed to replace will stay in production. NVIDIA hasn't confirmed any of it.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Advanced and Standard Voice modes end December 11 as OpenAI goes all-in on GPT-Live
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI will retire ChatGPT’s Advanced and Standard Voice modes on December 11, 2026, moving every voice user to the full-duplex GPT-Live model. The users who still prefer the older voices are pushing back — and OpenAI has reversed a voice retirement before.
